title: fix(components): a hand-authored form's select with multiple: true renders the multi-value widget and submits an array (objectui#11116)
body:
Fixes #11116
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

A hand-authored form field `{ type: 'select', multiple: true }` rendered the form renderer's built-in single-value select. `select` is a member of `BUILTIN_FIELD_TYPES`, so the bare spelling takes the built-in branch of `renderFieldComponent` (`BuiltinSelectControl`), which reads `multiple` nowhere. The object-bound path was never affected: `@object-ui/fields`' `mapFieldTypeToFormType` maps `select` + `multiple` to `field:multiselect` before the type reaches this renderer.

Measured on `origin/main` `8a5ae3d63` through the real `SchemaRenderer`, with `@object-ui/fields` registered, rendering the catalog example `fields-select/multi-select`: with `multiple: true` the field item held 1 `role="combobox"` and 0 option toggles, and the label pointed a `for` at the trigger. Without `multiple` the markup was the same. Submitting gave `{}`.

## The change

In `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`, a one-entry table `BUILTIN_MULTI_VALUE_WIDGETS` (`select` to `field:multiselect`) and `applyDeclaredArity` are applied where a field row computes `resolvedType`.

- **Why there, and not inside `renderFieldComponent`.** `resolveFieldLabelling`, `resolvesToRegisteredFieldWidget` and `rendersBuiltinSelectEmptyState` mirror the renderer's resolution. They now all see the routed id, so the label is associated the way `field:multiselect` declares (`labelling: 'group'`, by IDREF).
- **No second multi-select.** The widget is reached through `ComponentRegistry` at render time, like every other `field:*` widget. No import or dependency is added.
- **`multiple` is read truthy**, the way `mapFieldTypeToFormType` reads it, so both paths answer the same field the same way.

Measured after, same probe: 0 comboboxes, and 4 `aria-pressed` toggles inside a `role="group"` whose `aria-labelledby` is the label's id; the label has no `for`. Clicking two toggles and submitting gave `{"tags":["frontend","devops"]}`. Without `multiple`, the single combobox is unchanged.

## When `@object-ui/fields` is not registered

`field:multiselect` then resolves to nothing, so the routed field takes `renderFieldComponent`'s `default` branch. Measured: an `INPUT` with `type="text"`, and the label's `for` resolves to it. That is what an authored `field:multiselect` renders in the same host, which is the object-bound path's answer. The field no longer falls back to the single-value combobox. The pin asserts parity with the authored `field:multiselect` spelling rather than a literal element.

## Pins

- `packages/components/src/renderers/form/__tests__/form-builtin-select-multiple-11116.test.tsx` uses a probe widget. It pins: parity with `field:multiselect` when nothing is registered; routing to the registered widget; the group label association; the widget's array reaching `onSubmit`; and `multiple` absent or `false` keeping the built-in combobox and its `for`.
- `examples/schema-catalog/test/fields-select-multiple-11116.test.tsx` uses the real `SchemaRenderer` and the real `@object-ui/fields`. It pins: the example declares `multiple: true`; it renders one toggle per option inside a labelled group and no combobox; picking two submits an array; without `multiple` it is still the single-value select.

**Reverse verification.** The fix was committed first. The mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs`, whose anchor must hit (1 to 0, blob `a594c2831e54` to `1575184c442f`). Restore was proven by the blob matching HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Turning the routing condition into `false && multiple && …` gave 6 failed and 4 passed, the predicted split:
- **Red:** unregistered parity, routing, label association and the submitted array in the components pin; the toggles and the submitted array in the catalog pin.
- **Green:** the absent and `false` cases, the unchanged-without-`multiple` case, and the "declares multiple" case.

## Verification (all at HEAD `f9a8e349c`)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/src/renderers/form/` | 68 files, 465 passed, 17 skipped |
| `pnpm exec vitest run examples/schema-catalog/` | 35 files, 2203 passed |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` (after building the `@object-ui/fields^...` closure) | exit 0 |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` in components | the new test file is in the program |
| Catalog type-check, **narrowed** | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec eslint` on the three changed source/test files | 0 errors; none of the file's existing warnings lands in a changed hunk |
| `check-changeset-presence`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-lint-coverage`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
| `check:changeset-claims` | report-only; see Acceptance notes |

The catalog type-check was narrowed to a project holding only the new test file under the package's own `tsconfig.test.json` options, after building `@object-ui/fields`. The rest of the catalog's test program imports plugin packages this diff does not touch, and CI runs the full `type-check`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The catalog example's placeholder no longer renders.** The example's `placeholder: "Select tags..."` is not rendered any more, because `MultiSelectField` reads no `placeholder`. That is the widget the object-bound path already renders for the same declaration. Before this change the text showed only because the wrong widget rendered. Measured after: the string appears nowhere in the field item, and no element carries a `placeholder` attribute. It is not changed here, because it is outside this card's file surface. It is raised in the dev report.
- **A second copy of the table.** `BUILTIN_MULTI_VALUE_WIDGETS` is a one-entry copy of `MULTI_VALUE_FORM_TYPES` in `@object-ui/fields`, because `@object-ui/components` cannot import `fields`. Nothing re-derives the two against each other. The catalog pin notices a divergence only if it changes what the example renders.
- **Pending changesets re-read.** `check:changeset-claims` named three pending changesets that mention `form.tsx`. I re-read each paragraph against this diff and none is falsified. They cover the FormPage chain, the section-divider `className` read and the `description` wiring, and this change moves none of them.
- **Coordination with PR objectui#11115.** That PR declares `FormField.multiple` in `packages/types`. The files are disjoint. `FormField` carries an index signature today, so `fieldProps.multiple` type-checks with or without it.
